report.source_text: On laparoscopy, she was found to have 1.5 L of hemoperitoneum along with a normal-appearing uterus and left fallopian tube and a surgically absent right fallopian tube. The abdomen was thoroughly inspected with no identification of an ectopic pregnancy. A large expanding left retroperitoneal hematoma was visualized and noted to be pushing the sigmoid colon to the right pelvis (Fig. 1). The hematoma extended from below the left round ligament to above the pelvic brim. Blood was noted to be draining from the retroperitoneum into the pelvic cavity from pinpoint peritoneal openings, resulting in large volume hemoperitoneum. Intraoperative hemoglobin returned at 5.4 g/dL.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 38-year-old G6P2 woman with an etonogestrel implant presented with sudden onset abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding, acute abdomen, and vital signs suggestive of hypovolemia. Initial workup showed a beta-hCG of 12,712 mUI/mL, large amount of free fluid on FAST, and no intrauterine pregnancy on transvaginal ultrasound. Laparoscopy revealed 1.5 L hemoperitoneum, no ectopic pregnancy, and a large expanding left retroperitoneal hematoma with active bleeding from a left renal artery pseudoaneurysm. Endometrial biopsy showed inactive endometrium. Initial CT chest showed non-specific lesions. Subsequently, the patient developed a new 16-cm right perinephric hematoma requiring embolization, and CT chest revealed larger lesions suggestive of metastasis. The definitive diagnosis of metastatic choriocarcinoma was made via pathology from a craniotomy for brain metastases. The patient is undergoing chemotherapy for brain metastases, with a b-hCG of 9 one year after presentation.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Initial presentation with high beta-hCG (12,712 mUI/mL) and symptoms of acute abdomen and hypovolemia.
No intrauterine pregnancy noted on transvaginal ultrasound.
Laparoscopy ruled out ectopic pregnancy and revealed a large left retroperitoneal hematoma with hemoperitoneum.
Endometrial biopsy showed inactive endometrium, ruling out a primary uterine source for GTN.
CT angiogram identified active bleeding from a left renal artery pseudoaneurysm, explaining the retroperitoneal hematoma.
Development of a new 16-cm right perinephric hematoma and larger chest lesions suggestive of metastasis.
Definitive diagnosis of metastatic choriocarcinoma confirmed by pathology from craniotomy for brain metastases.
Patient undergoing chemotherapy for brain metastases with a b-hCG of 9 one year after initial presentation.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: No intrauterine pregnancy on TVUS (E001) and no ectopic pregnancy identified during laparoscopy (E002).
Endometrial biopsy showed fragments of inactive endometrium (E006).

remaining_uncertainties: Specific antecedent pregnancy type and the exact interval from that pregnancy to the diagnosis of GTN, which are factors for the WHO prognostic scoring.
